title: Kernel-aware mosaic phase scheduler: balancing latency and fair throughput
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current phase-splitting schedulers treat prefill and decode phases independently from kernel characteristics. This causes suboptimal kernel packing and QoS regressions when mixed workloads (short low-attention chat vs long high-attention summaries) share GPUs.

Proposal: Implement a 'mosaic' phase scheduler that jointly reasons about phase boundaries, kernel selection hints, and per-request fairness budgets. The scheduler will: (1) annotate requests with lightweight kernel affinity scores (e.g., memory-bound vs compute-bound, kv-cache pressure), (2) opportunistically co-locate compatible micro-phases to reduce kernel churn, and (3) enforce sliding fairness windows so latency-sensitive requests are prioritized without starving throughput-oriented batches.

Goals: Reduce kernel context-switching and prefill/decode thrashing, improve p95 latency for latency-sensitive classes by >= 15% on mixed workloads, retain throughput within 5% of baseline for batch-y workloads, and provide observable knobs for tradeoffs (aggressiveness, fairness window).
acceptance_criteria: p95 tail latency for latency-sensitive route improves by >= 15% on mixed synthetic workload (50% short chat, 50% long generation) compared to today
end-to-end throughput change <= 5% degradation for throughput-oriented route under same mixed workload
kernel-change rate (number of kernel switches per 1k tokens) decreases by >= 25% on benchmark traces
feature gated behind runtime flag and rolloutable by model/route
integration tests covering fairness windows and kernel hint propagation merged
dashboard panels added showing fairness window usage, kernel affinity distribution, and phase co-location ratios
updates: 2025-10-05: Spike prototype implemented in local runtime branch. Kernel-affinity computed from sequence length, kv cache usage, and attention sparsity estimate. Early microbenchmarks show kernel-change rate drop ~18% for small mixtures.

2025-10-12: Design review with runtime team. Decided to keep kernel-affinity heuristic simple (3 buckets) to avoid extra scheduling latency. Agreed on sliding fairness window of default 500ms per tenant route.

2025-10-22: Integration test harness added; simulating 10k mixed requests with realistic seq length distro (from prod traces). Observed p95 improvement 12% on prototype; identify edge case where long requests starve when window aggressively prioritizes latency traffic.
2025-10-29: Implemented decay-based backoff to prevent starvation. Benchmarks now show p95 improvement 18% while throughput drop ~3%.
2025-11-04: Created GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1892 (prototype + tests). Seeking review from kernel team for safe kernel hint propagation.
2025-11-09: Kernel team suggested adjusting hint semantics to be advisory only; updated scheduler to treat kernel hints as soft preferences and added fallback scoring. Updated unit tests.
2025-11-13: Canary ready. Added console panels and perf dashboards (link below). Preparing staged rollout plan — canary at 2 capacity regions with feature flag enabled for internal customers.
